AUDIT_B_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE_ARCHITECTURE.objective: Benchmark planned structure against established disciplines in Jewish Studies, Second Temple archaeology, Semitic philology, and Islamic studies.
disciplines_benchmarked: Hebrew Bible & Textual Criticism (Tov, Cross, Ulrich)
Second Temple Judaism & Sectarianism (Schiffman, Sanders, Charlesworth)
Medieval Jewish Philosophy & Kalam (Pines, Wolfson, Twersky)
Judeo-Islamic Symbiosis (Goitein, Bernard Lewis, Mark R. Cohen)
Modern Denominational Halakha & Reform (CCAR, CJLS, Poskim)
findings: Essential to reflect that Masoretic Text is a single textual family among multiple ancient traditions preserved at Qumran (Proto-MT, Pre-SP, LXX-Vorlage).
Crucial to differentiate between Tahrif al-Ma'na (misinterpretation) favored by early tafsir (Tabari, Razi) and Tahrif al-Nass (textual corruption) championed by Ibn Hazm.

Must preserve the halakhic reality that sacrifice ceased not out of doctrinal obsolescence, but due to halakhic prohibition of offering sacrifices outside the consecrated Temple Mount (Deut 12:13-14), replaced immediately by prayer (Hosea 14:3) and repentance.
AUDIT_B_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE_ARCHITECTURE.action_taken: Incorporated specific textual critical apparatuses and tripartite comparative analysis.
